subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity sizing & latency targets for FinPilot
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@finpilot.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated capacity sizing & latency targets for FinPilot

Sophie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same baseline. Please correct me if I mis-stated anything.

Call summary (what you told us)
- Primary workload: interactive analytics assistant for enterprise customers (dashboard queries + follow-up clarifications).
- Typical user turn: ~120–180 tokens; some longer summaries up to 400 tokens.
- Expected peak concurrency: 30–40 concurrent sessions initially; plan to scale later.
- Desired SLOs: p95 latency <= 350ms (streaming chunk delivery), p99 <= 700ms; cold-start target <= 1s.
- Streaming: yes — incremental token streaming required (clients render partial results).

Redwood recommended sizing (initial) — preliminary, for discussion
- Preferred GPU: H100 (best headroom for large context + throughput). Recommendation: 2 x H100 (reserved pool) to meet p95 targets with room for burst.
- Cost/perf tradeoff: A100 (4 x A100-40GB) can approximate similar throughput if you prioritize cost and accept higher utilization and slightly higher p95 on long-context requests. L4/Lite GPUs are not recommended for this workload due to streaming/tail latency constraints.
- Reserved throughput: we recommend reserving capacity to sustain ~1,000 tokens/sec peak (explained below) and a burst policy to +30% for short periods.

Performance assumptions used for sizing (tentative)
- Average response tokens: 150 tokens -> streaming at 20 tokens/sec typical.
- Peak concurrency 40 -> ~6 sustained responses/sec; combined token-rate targets motivate 1k tokens/sec reserve.
- Caching: request-level KV/prefix caching expected to cut token compute by ~15–30% for repeated prompts.

Validation plan (what Redwood will run)
1) Pre-PoC perf run: synthetic load test using your representative prompt set (we'll need the spreadsheet). Goal: measure steady-state p95/p99 and token throughput across H100 vs A100 config.
2) PoC (2–3 days): deploy dedicated pool, run live-ish traffic with your client (we mirror traffic pattern). Acceptance criteria: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms, sustained tokens/sec >= 900 for 10 minutes.
3) Post-PoC tuning: batching strategy, prefix caching, and KV config to lower unit cost while preserving SLOs.

Open items / asks for you
- Please share the FinPilot_SLO_requirements.xlsx (you mentioned it on the call).
- Confirm procurement timeline (PO/sig-off) and any firewall/VPC constraints for Private deployment.
- Any target date for the PoC window (we suggested Aug 9–13).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-proposal.pdf (high-level sizing + estimated reserved throughput), placeholder for the SLO spreadsheet.

Next steps
- Sophie: send SLO spreadsheet + confirm PoC week (FinPilot).
- Redwood (Vanessa + Rishi): prepare side-by-side H100 vs A100 perf plan and initial cost estimate.

Thanks — Connor

Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sophie — quick technical note on GPU sizing and streaming behavior from the infra side. Added some concrete numbers to help with procurement justification.

Short version (recommended): 2 x H100-80GB reserved pool. Why: headroom for long-context summaries (400+ tokens) and lower variance on p99. Single H100 is efficient but risks backpressure on sustained peaks.

H100 vs A100 vs L4 (rough guide)
- H100-80GB (recommended): best tail-latency and throughput. For your workload we estimate ~30–45 concurrent streaming sessions per H100 while hitting p95 <= 300–350ms when configured with our low-latency kernels and KV cache enabled.
- A100-40GB: cost-efficient at scale; expect to need ~2x A100s to match one H100 for streaming-heavy workloads due to memory+kernel efficiency. p95 will be ~10–20% higher on average for long-context requests.
- L4-class: good for low-cost embed/short-generation only. Not suitable for interactive streaming SLOs at scale.

Reserved throughput and concurrency planning
- We recommend reserving capacity for 1,000 tokens/sec as Connor suggested. Operationally we translate that to: 2 x H100 with autoscale headroom up to 3x for bursts (can be policy-driven).
- Concurrency policy: soft limit at 40 sessions, with queueing + fast-fallback to a smaller model (if you want cost-based graceful degradation).

Streaming flush/latency tradeoffs (your question)
- By default Redwood streams every ~50ms or every 16 tokens, whichever comes first, with a small Nagle-like coalescing window to balance network/CPU overhead vs jitter. We can tune to 20–30ms / 8–12 tokens for FinPilot if ultra-low jitter is required (but that increases CPU interrupts and slightly raises cost).

Perf validation plan (technical)
- Test matrix: run the representative prompt set across H100 vs A100 configs. Metrics: per-chunk latency distribution, end-to-end p95/p99, tokens/sec sustained, cold-start time after idle, memory pressure.
- Duration: 2 x 1-hour steady-state runs + a 30-minute burst run; followed by a 3-hour mixed-load soak if initial runs look good.
- Test owners: Redwood (Rishi, infra) + FinPilot dev lead on call to validate tokenization and prompt fidelity.

I'll prepare a short slide with these bullets and a rough cost delta for 2x H100 vs 4x A100 and share Monday.

-Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
